findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name F20's exact GitHub mechanism and field in the plan: the `description` field of `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}` (equivalently `gh repo edit --description`), and specify that exact-readback verification compares that `description` field while confirming `topics` and `homepage` are untouched.
evidence: Plan text: 'Use the authenticated GitHub metadata API under repository administration rights for F20, then verify exact readback through the same principal.'

Verified in-repo mechanism: infra/runbooks/github-mirror-lock.md:213 `gh repo edit navapbc/rebar --description "..."` sets the About/description; lines 203-204 `gh api -X PATCH repos/navapbc/rebar -F has_issues=false ...` patches repo metadata.

Verified prior GitHub REST usage: src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:167,182 call `https://api.github.com/repos/{repo}/...` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and document administration scope. Evidence class: Verified (observed).

The About-description update maps to the `description` field of PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}; the readback AC and the separate 'leaves topics/homepage unchanged' ACs both depend on comparing the correct field, which the plan does not name.
findings.finding: F20 names the integration surface only generically ('the authenticated GitHub metadata API') and does not pin the concrete endpoint/subcommand or the exact metadata field, even though the repo already documents the precise mechanism (`gh repo edit navapbc/rebar --description`, or `gh api -X PATCH repos/navapbc/rebar`). Naming the exact endpoint and the `description` field would make the operator's exact-readback verification unambiguous and prevent it from silently comparing the wrong field.
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan' bullet 'Use the authenticated GitHub metadata API under repository administration rights for F20, then verify exact readback through the same principal'; AC '[operator-attested] F20 updates the GitHub About description' and '[operator-attested] F20 receives exact readback verification before close'
scenarios: Operator runs the readback against a different metadata field (e.g. reads the repo object generically) and the check passes without confirming the description string actually changed.
Operator uses a `gh` form that also perturbs topics or homepage because the exact single-field call was not specified.
findings.suggested_fix: In the F20 bullet, replace 'the authenticated GitHub metadata API' with the concrete call, e.g.: 'Update the About text through the `description` field of `PATCH /repos/navapbc/rebar` (equivalently `gh repo edit navapbc/rebar --description`) under repository administration rights, then read back `description`, `topics`, and `homepage` through the same principal and assert only `description` changed.'
